key: And if I say: ‘I will not make mention of Him, Nor speak any more in His name’, Then there is in my heart as it were a burning fire Shut up in my bones, And I weary myself to hold it in, But cannot.
s: After his night in Pashhur’s stocks, Jeremiah complains that the LORD’s word has made him a laughing-stock; Rashi, on 20:9, reads the fire as the prophecy itself, which compels him against his will to keep going on God’s mission.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Jeremiah 20:9, at [419,9]). Plain sense faithful: 20:3 has Pashhur bring him out of the stocks on the morrow, 20:7 to 8 the complaint of being a laughing-stock and the word of the LORD made a reproach; no four-word repeat of the key. Rashi on 20:9 glosses the first lemma as his heart telling him not to go on His mission any more and the second as the prophecy like a burning fire, so that against his will he must go (consistent with his 20:7 gloss, going against his will). The reading (the fire is the prophecy, compelling him against his will to keep going on the mission) is carried by those words without drift. Entry passes entry-check.
